commentary_title: Weak Asian demand to keep VLCC rates soft
commentary_summary: The VLCC tonne-miles index declined for a third consecutive week ending at 102.5 points, lower by close to 4 points. There is weakness in the tonnage demand, especially towards the East, where a lower-than-expected Chinese demand is hampering trade for the winter months. The TD3C route also declined further and is likely to remain weak even in the next week. | Markets started out slow but gained some momentum towards the middle of the week towards the West of Suez. The MEG to UKC route saw an uptick in rates as an increase in cargoes resulted in a requirement for more tonnage. The market activity for next week however seems to be on the grimmer side due to the possibility of the weakness in the smaller size segments weighing down on VLCC rates.
